name: Ransom Letter
summary: The Ransom Letter is a threat from the thieves holding Narain’s book in Tanaris. Its cut-and-pasted words demand money and a meeting alone.

sections.title: A Cut-Out Threat
sections.body: Narain’s missing book brings a ransom demand to Tanaris. The letter’s words are cut from different typefaces and glued onto parchment. It promises the book will be returned if the demands are met, then sets out detailed instructions across three pages. The message ends with a blunt order: bring the money and come alone.

sections.title: Narain’s Anger
sections.body: When Narain reads the ransom letter, his face turns bright red. The gnome vows to teach the kidnappers what it means to meddle with a psychic. His stolen book has become a matter of anger as well as payment.

faq.answer: The letter does not name its writer. It says that the kidnappers have Narain’s book and demands money in exchange.
The book belongs to Narain, a gnome in Tanaris.
The kidnappers demand money and order the recipient to come alone.

faq.q: Why is the letter made from cut-out words?
faq.answer: Its text is made from different typefaces glued onto parchment. The letter gives no reason for this method.
Narain’s face turns bright red, and he vows to teach the kidnappers a lesson.

angles.text: As a gnome, you may recognize Narain’s pride in his psychic abilities. The stolen book and ransom threat leave him furious.
